documents.unit: University Information Services (with Office of General Counsel)
documents.title: Guidelines for the Georgetown Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Landing page of University Information Services guidelines with six principles (accountability, transparency, fairness, privacy, security, IP) and two warnings about bots and unapproved tools. It sets conditions on AI use, not a teaching rule.
documents.stance_why: The page is a university-wide set of principles. It never bans AI or assigns the decision to instructors; it recognizes the "transformative potential of AI" and attaches conditions (accountability, disclosure if required, privacy, IP, no unapproved tools for university data), so permit with conditions.

units.why: The sentence says "Use of AI by members of the Georgetown community must remain aligned with current university policies", an institution-wide scope rule binding everyone, so actor all, phase general, must. P56 (framework) fits because it sets no allow/ban position.
units.anchor: Use of AI by members of the Georgetown community must remain aligned with current university

units.why: The guidelines state they are "not intended as legal advice or an exhaustive set of best practices", a statement of the document's scope and status; general, informs, P56 (framework preamble) fits better than P61 because it does not define AI.
units.anchor: not intended as legal advice or an exhaustive set of best practices

units.why: "These guidelines may be updated over time to reflect changes in the regulatory environment, industry standards, and technology" says the policy is provisional, so P54, addressed to the university (admin), over-time, informs.
units.anchor: may be updated over time to reflect changes in the regulatory environment

units.why: The definition "Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence that creates new content by learning from existing data" sets what the guidelines cover, so P61, general, informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence that creates new content

units.why: "Do not allow unfamiliar bots to join your meetings" is a directive to everyone about AI bots; the nearest type is P50 (prefer vetted tools, protect data) because the concern is unvetted tools. Must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: Do not allow unfamiliar bots to join your meetings

units.why: "Do not upload, input, or analyze university data in an AI tool that is not approved by UIS" limits data sharing to vetted tools. P50 fits (protect data, vetted tools); P49 only covers students uploading course materials.
units.anchor: Do not upload, input, or analyze university data in an AI tool that is not

units.why: The accountability principle says members "are accountable for the work product or decisions resulting from their use of AI"; this is ownership of output (P29), binding all, must.
units.anchor: are accountable for the work product or decisions resulting from their use of AI

units.why: "Use of AI tools must be disclosed if prescribed by law, university policy, or publisher requirements" is a conditional disclosure duty, so P24, must, during-work. Disclosure is a condition on allowed use, so unit_stance is permit.
units.anchor: Use of AI tools must be disclosed if prescribed by law, university policy, or publisher

units.why: "should be mindful that AI outputs may sometimes contain bias" names bias as a concern, so P53; P31 (verify output) does not fit because no verification duty is stated. Should.
units.anchor: should be mindful that AI outputs may sometimes contain bias

units.why: "must respect the privacy of others' personally identifiable information" protects personal data when using AI, so P50, must, all.
units.anchor: must respect the privacy of others' personally identifiable information

units.why: "should take steps to maintain the security and integrity of Georgetown resources" is a security duty. No type covers security of institutional systems (P50 is personal data and vetted tools), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: should take steps to maintain the security and integrity of Georgetown resources
units.uncovered_note: Maintain the security and integrity of university resources when using AI

units.why: "should respect and preserve intellectual property rights as they use AI tools" is an IP rule, so P52, should, all.
units.anchor: should respect and preserve intellectual property rights as they use AI tools

documents.unit: Center for New Designs in Learning and Scholarship (CNDLS), AI Toolkit
documents.title: Developing course policies - AI Toolkit
tiers: Permit AI tools at certain stages
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance for writing syllabus AI policies. Offers three approaches, faculty examples including a CS course, policies by assignment, AI-assisted grading principles and advice on suspected violations.
documents.stance_why: CNDLS says whether AI is allowed "is answered by individual course policies" and offers three approaches with sample language, so it sets no stance itself and delegates with named approaches.

units.uncovered_note: Students are responsible for knowing and following the AI rules their professors set

notes: Coder A. Only the three included university-layer documents were coded; there is no school or computing-layer document. CS-specific content appears only as faculty example 5 (Nathan Schneider, Computer Science) inside the CNDLS page. The CNDLS page was coded as quoted sample and example policies; each example is exemplar language, not a binding rule. Repeated text (Honor Council quote, sample disclosure statement, AI-grading paragraph) is coded once.
